Phase 7 (mockup-driven desktop UI gap, plus one backend story) is in progress: windows-desktop-prestart-lab-gate is done (PreStartGateDialog); windows-desktop-import-lab-file is done (ImportLabDialog in import_lab.py + lab_file.py, 'Import Lab File…' button in main_window.py; conflict-free imports auto-start, conflicts hand over to PreStartGateDialog; bundled sample labs; recent-files list; awaiting a Windows smoke run); windows-desktop-in-app-dialogs is in_progress with the file-picker AC now met and only the Dashboard Delete / Lifecycle Reset ACs open. stories.title: Subnet Conflict Detection and Resolution
stories.notes: Added and implemented 2026-10-23 after the first Windows smoke run of the import flow failed at start with Docker's 'Pool overlaps with other one on this address space' (Tigre/06 #13; was Tigre/11 proposal S-16). Core: src/practicum/networks.py (find_subnet_conflicts / recommend_subnet from 10.90.0.0/16 / move_subnet keeping host offsets), DockerRuntime.list_networks() (docker network ls + inspect, parses IPAM subnets, practicum.lab_id label, attached containers) and remove_network() (docker rm -f containers, then network rm), LabService.check_networks / apply_subnet_recommendation / remove_leftover_network, routes GET /labs/{id}/networks, POST /labs/{id}/networks/apply-recommendation, POST /labs/{id}/networks/remove-leftover (409 for no recommendation / not a leftover), models DockerNetworkInfo, SubnetConflict (reasons overlaps_other_lab | overlaps_leftover | overlaps_docker_network), NetworkCheckResult (error field when Docker is unreachable), and LabDefinition now rejects overlapping subnets within a lab. Desktop: ApiClient.check_networks / apply_subnet_recommendation / remove_leftover_network / reset_lab; PreStartGateDialog gained a 'Network Conflicts' group (owner text per reason; fixes 'Remove leftover' and 'Reset <lab>' via confirm(destructive=True), 'Use <subnet>' which re-renders the topology and warns that the manual may mention old addresses; Start requires both port and network checks to have answered clean); ImportLabDialog's check stage is now 'Checking host ports and networks…' and hands over to the gate on subnet conflicts. Tests: core +27 (test_networks 11, test_network_conflicts_api 11 with a FakeRuntime, test_runtime +5), desktop +17 (gate +8, api_client +7, import +2). Verified end-to-end in the sandbox against a stateful fake docker CLI: the user's exact failure reproduced, then all three fixes (remove leftover, reset owner, use subnet) cleared it and the lab started. Not yet verified on Windows with real Docker Desktop.

acceptance_criteria.text: A lab whose subnet overlaps an existing Docker network is reported by GET /labs/{lab_id}/networks with the owner identified and a recommended subnet, before any Start is attempted.
The pre-start gate blocks Start while subnet conflicts exist and shows the owner of each.
Removing a leftover from the gate deletes that network and its containers and clears the conflict; the lab definition is unchanged.
Resetting the owning lab from the gate clears the conflict.
Applying the recommended subnet moves the network and its addresses, the topology shown in the gate updates, and the user is told the manual may still mention the old addresses.
Importing a lab with a subnet conflict stops at the gate instead of failing at start.
Overlapping subnets within one lab are rejected at validation.

stories.title: Open a Shell on a Lab Node
stories.notes: Added and implemented 2026-10-23 (was Tigre/11 proposal S-11, P0) after the user's first started lab was unusable: they tried `ssh 10.93.1.0` from Windows - node addresses live inside Docker Desktop's VM and the nodes run no SSH server. MVP: desktop/src/practicum_desktop/node_shell.py (shell_command = docker exec -it <container> sh -c 'command -v bash && exec bash || exec sh'; open_node_shell launches it in a new console - Windows: cmd.exe /k with CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE so errors stay visible; Linux: first of x-terminal-emulator/gnome-terminal/konsole/xterm; otherwise returns the command for copying). ApiClient.get_status -> StatusResult{lab_status, resources:[ResourceStatusInfo], containers}. main_window.py gained a 'Lab Nodes' table (Node / Container / State / Open shell) filled from GET /labs/{id}/status on selection and after Start; button enabled only for running containers; status line explains addresses are reachable only inside the lab. Default window size raised to 560x760. Probe kit lab 1's manual now says to use Open shell. Tests: desktop +12 (test_node_shell 5, test_main_window +4, test_api_client +3) -> 134. Rendered offscreen against the fake-docker API. Not yet verified on Windows (CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE + cmd /k with Docker Desktop).

stories.title: Pre-Start Readiness Gate
stories.notes: Implemented as PreStartGateDialog (desktop/src/practicum_desktop/prestart_gate.py): loads GET /labs/{lab_id}/preview and GET /labs/{lab_id}/ports in parallel, shows name/description/author/version, required images, estimated CPU/memory, a read-only topology table (node/network/address), a manual step count, and a port-conflicts table with per-row 'Use <port>' buttons. Start Lab is disabled while conflicts remain and re-enables once resolved. Wired into main_window.py's existing Start button (which now opens this dialog instead of calling start_lab directly); the main window's Start button and inline port-conflict table no longer gate on conflicts themselves, since the dialog is now the single authority for that. Required extending PreviewResult/get_preview in api_client.py to parse required_images/estimated_resources/topology fields the API already returned but the desktop client was discarding. 11 new tests (7 dialog + 4 extended api_client assertions implicitly covered by existing suite), all passing; PORT_CONFLICT_REASONS moved to api_client.py as a shared constant to avoid duplicating it between main_window.py and this dialog. Not yet reachable from the Labs Dashboard or Import flows since those don't exist yet (windows-desktop-labs-dashboard, windows-desktop-import-lab-file) - both should open this same dialog rather than re-implementing the gate once built. Update 2026-10-23: the gate now also checks Docker subnet overlaps (GET /labs/{id}/networks) in a 'Network Conflicts' group with Remove leftover / Reset <lab> / Use <subnet> fixes; Start requires both the port and the network check to be clean (runtime-subnet-conflicts).

acceptance_criteria.text: The screen shows lab name, description, required images, estimated resources, and read-only topology.
Port conflicts block Start until resolved, and applying a recommendation re-checks and clears that conflict.
A lab with zero conflicts shows a clear ready-to-start state and an immediately-enabled Start button.
Canceling this screen does not start, modify, or delete the lab.

stories.title: Import Lab File and Launch
stories.notes: Implemented 2026-10-23 as ImportLabDialog in desktop/src/practicum_desktop/import_lab.py, opened from the new 'Import Lab File…' button in main_window.py. The dialog is the in-app 'Open Lab File' modal from the mockup (importModal): a list of recently imported files (QSettings key recent_lab_files, newest first, max 8, missing files shown greyed) plus the sample labs bundled in the package (desktop/src/practicum_desktop/samples/*.json, byte-identical copies of examples/ guarded by a test), and 'Browse computer…' which opens QFileDialog.getOpenFileName (filter *.json) - the single sanctioned native dialog; picking a file there continues immediately. The same dialog then becomes the staged progress view (importingOverlay): Reading lab file -> Importing lab definition (POST /labs/import via the new ApiClient.import_lab/ImportLabResult) -> Checking host ports (GET /labs/{id}/ports) -> Starting containers (POST /labs/{id}/start). Conflict-free labs start with no further clicks; labs with conflicts (or an unanswerable port check) return gate_required and MainWindow opens PreStartGateDialog for them, so the gate stays the only authority for starting with conflicts. File problems are caught before any API call by lab_file.read_lab_file: missing file, directory, >5 MB, non-UTF-8, JSON syntax error with line/column, non-object JSON, and .zip (no bundle format exists yet - rejected with 'choose the .json export' guidance). API schema errors are listed inline as 'nodes[0].image: Field required' lines (lab_file.format_issue); unsupported schema_version majors (e.g. 2.0) are now rejected server-side by LabDefinition with a readable message. If the API is down the dialog shows a blocked banner pointing at the main window's status/Retry instead of a generic failure. After the dialog closes MainWindow refreshes GET /labs, selects the imported lab, shows 'imported and started' (or 'imported - use Start when ready'), and opens the manual flyout when started - today's equivalent of the running view until windows-desktop-embedded-lab-view exists; re-point _apply_pending_selection when it does. Duplicate imports create a new lab each time (API behaviour; Tigre/09 Q-1 still open). Also fixed on the way: ApiClient.start_lab now uses a 900 s lifecycle timeout (Tigre/06 #3) with a specific timeout message; the runtime and docker_status now treat any OSError from the docker CLI (e.g. PermissionError) as a structured failure instead of a 500 / a dead startup thread. Tests: desktop 105 (+56: test_lab_file 19, test_import_lab 21, test_main_window 7, test_api_client +8, test_docker_status +1; shared tests/qt_helpers.py), core 104 (+4). Exercised end-to-end in a Linux sandbox against a live API (PySide6 offscreen): valid import, schema 2.0 rejection, multi-error file, forced port conflict -> gate, conflict-free -> start failure surfaced with guidance. NOT yet manually verified on Windows - needs one smoke run with Docker Desktop (native picker look, auto-start landing, recent list). Update 2026-10-23 (after the first Windows smoke run hit Tigre/06 #13): the check stage is now 'Checking host ports and networks…' - a subnet overlap with an existing Docker network (typically a leftover from an earlier session) hands over to the gate, which can fix it, instead of failing at start (runtime-subnet-conflicts).

acceptance_criteria.text: The user can select a lab file via a file-open affordance.

The imported lab appears in the Labs Dashboard list afterward, whether or not it was started in the same flow.

Replaces the current webbrowser.open(...)-based external launch with an in-app embedded view (likely QWebEngineView from the already-bundled PySide6 QtWebEngineWidgets), docked beside the existing Lab Manual flyout. Reference design: screen-running's browser-pane in practicum-mockups.html.

acceptance_criteria.text: A lab with one browser-accessible node shows that node's interface embedded in the app, not in an external browser.
A lab with multiple browser-accessible nodes lets the user pick which one to view.
The instructions flyout can be opened and closed without losing the embedded view's state.
An open-in-system-browser option is available from the embedded view.

stories.title: Visual Topology Builder (Basic)
stories.notes: New story. Upgrades the existing table-based DesignerDialog (designer-add-nodes/designer-add-networks/designer-connect-nodes-networks, all done) to a card-based Machines/Network-Topology/Networks layout with no changes to validation or the underlying data model. Deliberately scoped below future-roadmap/advanced-designer-features/advanced-visual-topology-designer.md (drag-and-drop canvas, auto-layout), which remains a candidate paid feature per open-core-boundary.md. Reference design: screen-custom in practicum-mockups.html.

acceptance_criteria.text: Adding a machine shows it as a card with its id and image.
Adding a network shows it in the networks panel with its id and subnet.
Connecting a machine to a network updates the topology view to show that connection and its subnet label.
Existing Validate and Save behavior, including error messages, is unchanged.

stories.title: Image Pull and Start Progress
stories.notes: New story, the one backend exception in the otherwise desktop-UI-only phase-7 backlog. DockerRuntime.start() (src/practicum/runtime.py) shells out to `docker run` per container via subprocess and blocks on the final exit code only; it surfaces no incremental pull/start progress today. The mockup's start/import loading sequences currently fake this with a fixed-duration timer. Likely needs an explicit `docker pull` step per node plus parsing Docker's streamed JSON progress, surfaced through a richer GET /labs/{lab_id}/status rather than a new transport.

acceptance_criteria.text: Lab status exposes a distinguishable in-progress state per node while starting, separate from running/stopped/error.
When a node's image must be pulled, its status includes enough information for the desktop app to show real percentage-style progress.
When a node's image is already local, its status does not show pull progress and moves directly to container startup.
A failed pull or container start is reported against the specific node, with a message distinct from a generic failure.
